questions.question: Start at 7. Count on 3 more. What number do you land on?
questions.explain: Start at 7 and count on: 8, 9, 10. You land on 10. A common mistake is counting 7 as the first number — don't count the starting number!

questions.question: Start at 12. Count back 4. What number do you land on?
questions.explain: Start at 12 and count back: 11, 10, 9, 8. You land on 8. A common mistake is counting 12 itself as the first step — start counting after it.

questions.question: 8 + 4. Count on from 8. What is the sum?
questions.explain: Start at 8 and count on 4: 9, 10, 11, 12. The sum is 12. Don't count 8 as the first step, and don't go backwards when you are adding.

questions.question: 5 + 7. Count on from the bigger number. What is the sum?
questions.explain: The bigger number is 7. Start at 7 and count on 5: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. The sum is 12. Always start counting on from the bigger number.

questions.question: You have 9 stickers. You get 5 more. Start at 9 and count on. How many stickers do you have now?
questions.explain: Start at 9 and count on 5: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. You have 14 stickers. A common mistake is counting 9 as the first number — start counting after it!

questions.question: You have 13 pencils. You use 5 of them. Start at 13 and count back. How many are left?
questions.explain: Start at 13 and count back 5: 12, 11, 10, 9, 8. You have 8 pencils left. Don't count 13 as the first step when counting back.

questions.question: Mia has 11 blocks. She adds 6 more. She starts at 11 and counts on. What number does she land on?
questions.explain: Start at 11 and count on 6: 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. Mia lands on 17. A common mistake is counting 11 itself as the first number.

questions.question: Tom has 7 apples. He gets 5 more, then gives 3 away. Start at 7, count on 5, then count back 3. How many apples does he have?
questions.explain: First: start at 7, count on 5 to get 12. Then: start at 12, count back 3 to get 9. Don't count the starting number as your first step!

questions.question: You start at 10. Count on 5, then count back 4 from that number. What number do you end on?
questions.explain: First: 10 + 5 = 15. Then: start at 15 and count back 4: 14, 13, 12, 11. You end on 11. A common mistake is going the wrong way on the count-back step.

questions.question: Lily does 9 + 5. She starts at 9 and counts: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. What did Lily do wrong?
questions.explain: Lily counted 9 as her first step. She should have started counting after 9: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. The answer is 14, not 13.

questions.question: You have 14 marbles. A friend gives you 3 more. Start at 14 and count on 3. How many marbles do you have?
questions.explain: Start at 14 and count 3 more: 15, 16, 17. Don't count 14 as the first number in your count.

questions.question: You have 16 blocks. You give 4 to your little brother. Start at 16 and count back 4. How many blocks are left?
questions.explain: Start at 16 and count back 4: 15, 14, 13, 12. Don't count 16 as your first step, and don't count up.

questions.question: Mia has 15 crayons. She uses 5. Start at 15 and count back 5. How many crayons are left?
questions.explain: Start at 15 and count back 5: 14, 13, 12, 11, 10. The trap is counting 15 as your very first step.

questions.question: You have 8 tokens. You find 7 more under your seat. Start at 8 and count on 7. How many tokens do you have?
questions.explain: Start at 8 and count 7 more: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. Count only what comes after the starting number.

questions.question: Jake has 9 rocks. He finds 5 more on the beach. Then he gives 3 to his sister. Start at 9, count on 5, then count back 3. How many rocks does Jake have?
questions.explain: First count on 5 from 9 to get 14. Then count back 3 from 14 to get 11. Don't count the starting number in your count.

questions.question: You have 10 cookies. You eat 4. Your mom bakes 6 more. Start at 10, count back 4, then count on 6. How many cookies do you have?
questions.explain: First count back 4 from 10 to get 6. Then count on 6 from 6 to get 12. Watch your direction — back first, then on.

questions.question: You have some apples. You pick 4 more and now have 15. How many did you have before? Count back from 15.
questions.explain: Count back 4 from 15: 14, 13, 12, 11. You had 11 apples before. Don't count 15 as your first step.

questions.question: Sam does 14 − 5. He counts: 14, 13, 12, 11, 10. He says the answer is 10. What did he do wrong?
options: He counted up instead of back.
He said 14 as his first count.
He went one step too far back.
questions.explain: When you count back 5 from 14, you go: 13, 12, 11, 10, 9. The answer is 9. You only count the steps after the starting number.
